question: Can one oneDNN subgroup reproduce natural-M1's eight 64-K FP32 chains in registers, then reduce them in the proven order, without the eight K-subgroups and SLM reduction that made R142/R143 too slow?

evidence_base.observed_onednn_order: With local-K interleave ki64 and wgK=8, lane p starts at p*64, advances by 512, and lane 0 adds p=1 through p=7 in ascending order. R142 reproduced this exactly on both dominant production shapes.

source.build_mode: ONEDNN_DEV_MODE=ON for forced strategy selection and generator diagnostics

fixed_implementation.strategy_modifier: Add one explicit kri64 modifier. It is invalid unless the K loop unroll is exactly 512, the kernel is systolic FP32 accumulation, local/global K parallelism is absent, C repacking is absent, and K is divisible by 512.
fixed_implementation.register_buffers: Allocate exactly eight C register buffers before GEMM register allocation. Ordinary strategies retain one buffer and unchanged behavior.
fixed_implementation.routing: Keep the ordinary 32-K BDPAS/load cadence. For each generated outer product at compile-time K offset h, write to C buffer floor((h mod 512)/64). Thus each buffer receives its 64 contiguous K positions once per 512-K macro-step.
fixed_implementation.reduction: After the K loop and before offsets/post-ops/output conversion, execute C0 += C1, then +=C2, ..., +=C7 in FP32 register order using the existing register-layout mapper.
fixed_implementation.forbidden: No K workgroups, SLM, barriers, padding, allocation/copy wrapper, atomics, global scratch, custom SYCL GEMM, server build, or collective experiment.

m16_n4_wg8x1.purpose: Lowest-register feasibility arm derived from the exact natural source-M4 anchor; 32 C GRFs before A/B and temporaries.

m16_n16_wg4x2.purpose: Serving candidate with 128 C GRFs and an eight-subgroup 64x32 workgroup output tile.

m16_n16_wg4x4.purpose: Wider scheduling arm with the same per-subgroup register footprint and a 64x64 workgroup output tile.

ordered_stages: Implement the narrow modifier and register-buffer path in a clean pinned oneDNN tree; make a cumulative patch and record its hash.
Build the smallest extension target without device access. Parse/generate m16_n4_wg8x1 first; record any generator exception or register-allocation failure.
Only if the smallest arm generates, parse/generate the two 16x16 arms. Invalid arms are recorded and not substituted.
Only generated arms run on B70 0000:03:00.0 in fresh bounded containers, smallest first, with health checks between cases.
Identity precedes timing. No endpoint or second-GPU use is authorized by this preregistration.

operator_screen.identity: Every complete output must equal concatenated natural oneDNN M1 rows. M512 prefixes, M128 repeat and seeded permutation, and M168-to-M200 random-padding content must also be bitwise exact.
operator_screen.timing: Ten warmups and five samples of 100 synchronized calls at M2, M64, M128, M168, and M256 against natural oneDNN.
operator_screen.stability: No timed sample max/min ratio may exceed 1.15.

gates.source: The modifier must reject every unsupported condition and leave the ordinary path byte-for-byte source-equivalent outside its guards.
gates.candidate: Generation, identity, and stability are independently required. A candidate proceeds only if it is <=1.15x natural on both shapes at M2, M64, and M128 and <=2.0x at M168 and M256.
gates.composition: A row-count threshold composition may use independently exact candidates only when the frozen 16:64 attention-QKV:gate-up model is <=1.03x natural at M2, M64, and M128.
gates.on_pass: Expand only the fastest exact passing candidate or composition to all six production shapes and apply the <=1.03 frozen all-shape decode model before any serving build.
gates.on_failure: Preserve R142 as the executable arithmetic reference. Record whether failure is register capacity, generated-code size, identity, or latency; do not resume direct K-subgroup/SLM geometry sweeps and do not begin collective optimization.

abort_conditions: any current-boot Xe fault, CAT error, reset, coredump, device loss, timeout, or hung stage visible to the available health interfaces
either B70 is not normal before or after a device case
any unregistered strategy, arithmetic/reduction order, candidate substitution, server launch, or second-GPU use
